Let’s talk about Chapter 8: The Challenge of Consistency—Facing Setbacks and Self-Doubt.
You know, no journey of change is ever smooth sailing. Even with the best intentions, old habits have this sneaky way of creeping back in—especially when you’re stressed, tired, or just not sure what comes next. Your mind starts whispering things like, “This is just who I am,” or, “Change is way too hard.” Sound familiar?
Imagine a young professional, really trying to stick to her new agreements. But then her boss starts piling on the work. That old habit of saying yes to everything? It takes over. She finds herself exhausted, resentful, and wondering if she’s failed. And honestly, the urge to give up can feel overwhelming.
Here’s something to pay attention to—setbacks aren’t proof that you’ve failed. They’re actually invitations to deepen your practice. These agreements you’re working with? They’re not about being perfect. They’re about being present. Every time you notice yourself slipping, you get a fresh chance to remember your intention, forgive yourself, and try again.
And let’s be real—self-doubt is always lurking around on this path. Your mind starts questioning if real change is even possible. Will those old stories ever really fade away? In moments like these, it helps to remind yourself that transformation rarely moves in a straight line. There’ll be days when everything clicks, and days when nothing makes sense. Moments of progress, and moments when it feels like you’re back at square one.
Think about a parent who’s trying hard to break the cycle of criticism with their child. But in a stressful moment, the old words come out—the same ones they heard as a kid. The guilt stings, and disappointment sets in. But rather than giving up, they choose to apologize, to explain, and to try again. And you know what? When the child sees that kind of vulnerability, they learn something powerful: mistakes are just part of being human, and love is big enough to hold all our imperfections.
Having support makes a huge difference. Whether it’s a trusted friend, a mentor, or a whole community of people on the same journey, encouragement and perspective help so much. Sharing those ups and downs makes the struggle feel normal—and the small victories feel worth celebrating.
Over time, you’ll notice the setbacks don’t happen as often. And when they do, you bounce back faster. Your mind starts to realize it’s safe to let go of those old agreements, and new ways of being begin to feel possible.
So, here’s the key takeaway: the journey isn’t about never falling. It’s about learning to rise again, each time, with a little more ease and a lot more compassion.
